title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: A teammate asks how to tell whether a system built on a language model is a workflow or an agent. Which question separates the two?

options.text: How many times the model is called for one request
Whether the system is given tools it can call
Whether the code or the model decides the next step
How large and capable the underlying model is

items.stem: A makerspace assistant handles every request like this. Step 1: one model call labels the question 'booking' or 'manual'. Step 2: Python code runs `if label == 'booking': book_flow() else: manual_flow()`. Step 3: each flow is a fixed list of steps, some of which call tools, and a final model call writes the reply. Which description is correct?

options.text: A workflow: the code fixes the possible paths, and the model only supplies a label
An agent: the model's label picks the path, so the model controls the flow
A workflow, but only if no step in either flow calls a tool
An agent: it makes several model calls in a row for one request

items.stem: The booking part of the assistant needs three things done for each booking: check the calendar, check the student's training status, then book the slot. Your sponsor's model budget is small. Which design should you pick for this part, and why?

options.text: An agent, because a model that chooses its own steps books more accurately
A workflow, because only a workflow can call the calendar and booking tools
An agent, because it makes fewer model calls than a workflow on simple requests
A workflow, because the steps are known ahead, so code can run them cheaply

items.stem: The assistant must book equipment, and also help students with open-ended equipment problems. Where should an agent loop sit, if anywhere?

options.text: Over the whole assistant, with the booking steps written into its prompt
Only on the troubleshooting path, with code sending bookings to a fixed workflow
Nowhere, because a workflow with enough branches can handle any problem a student raises
Only on the booking path, because bookings involve the most tool calls

items.stem: Which request to the makerspace assistant is the best fit for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: "Check whether the laser cutter is free Friday at 3 pm and, if so, book it."
"Show me the safety rules in the band saw manual before my session."
"Find a machine that can make this part, compare options, and book one."
"Which of my three training certificates expire this term?"

items.stem: Which of these is a true advantage of a fixed workflow over an agent?

options.text: Its steps are set in code, so a request follows the same path each time
It handles requests nobody planned for, because the code adapts to them
It needs no model calls, because the code does all of the work
It gives more accurate answers than an agent on open-ended requests
